--!strict
-- Snapshot.lua -- delta checkpoints of a whole Machine.
--
-- A machine is a graph of plain tables, scalars and buffers plus methods that
-- live on metatables and on instance fields (closures). Saving closures is
-- not possible, so a checkpoint is a *delta against a freshly built machine*:
-- the caller supplies a factory that builds the same machine (same ROMs, same
-- base disk images, same config) and capture() walks the live graph and the
-- fresh one in lock-step, recording only scalar fields that differ, tables the
-- fresh machine lacks, and 4 KiB pages of buffers that differ. apply() builds
-- nothing itself: it overlays that delta onto another fresh machine, leaving
-- every function (including instance-patched ones) untouched.
--
-- Not captured: functions, metatables, userdata other than buffers, tables
-- used as keys. State that lives only in a closure's upvalues is therefore not
-- captured; the determinism test in tests/SnapshotTests.lua is the check that
-- a given machine configuration has none.

local Snapshot = {}

local PAGE = 4096
local MAGIC = "RVPCSNAP1"
local ZERO_PAGE = string.rep("\0", PAGE)

local pack = string.pack
-- string.unpack is typed as returning unknowns; every format used here yields
-- numbers (the one string result is only passed through as `any`).
local unpack = string.unpack :: (fmt: string, s: string, init: number?) -> ...number

local encodeValue: (v: any, out: { string }, seen: { [any]: boolean }) -> ()

local function encodeBuffer(b: buffer, out: { string })
	local len = buffer.len(b)
	local pages: { string } = {}
	local count = 0
	local off = 0
	while off < len do
		local n = math.min(PAGE, len - off)
		local s = buffer.readstring(b, off, n)
		if s ~= string.sub(ZERO_PAGE, 1, n) then
			count += 1
			pages[#pages + 1] = pack("<I4", off // PAGE)
			pages[#pages + 1] = s
		end
		off += PAGE
	end
	out[#out + 1] = pack("<I4I4", len, count)
	for _, p in pages do
		out[#out + 1] = p
	end
end

function encodeValue(v: any, out: { string }, seen: { [any]: boolean })
	local t = typeof(v)
	if t == "boolean" then
		out[#out + 1] = if v then "T" else "F"
	elseif t == "number" then
		out[#out + 1] = "N" .. pack("<d", v)
	elseif t == "string" then
		out[#out + 1] = "S" .. pack("<s4", v)
	elseif t == "buffer" then
		out[#out + 1] = "B"
		encodeBuffer(v, out)
	elseif t == "table" then
		if seen[v] then
			error("snapshot: cycle inside a table the fresh machine does not have")
		end
		seen[v] = true
		local keys: { { any } } = {}
		for k, val in v do
			local kt = typeof(k)
			local vt = typeof(val)
			if
				(kt == "string" or kt == "number" or kt == "boolean")
				and vt ~= "function"
				and vt ~= "thread"
				and vt ~= "userdata"
				and vt ~= "vector"
			then
				keys[#keys + 1] = { k, val }
			end
		end
		out[#out + 1] = "{" .. pack("<I4", #keys)
		for _, kv in keys do
			encodeValue(kv[1], out, seen)
			encodeValue(kv[2], out, seen)
		end
		seen[v] = nil
	else
		out[#out + 1] = "Z"
	end
end

local decodeValue: (data: string, pos: number) -> (any, number)

function decodeValue(data: string, pos: number): (any, number)
	local tag = string.sub(data, pos, pos)
	pos += 1
	if tag == "Z" then
		return nil, pos
	elseif tag == "T" then
		return true, pos
	elseif tag == "F" then
		return false, pos
	elseif tag == "N" then
		local n, p = unpack("<d", data, pos)
		return n, p
	elseif tag == "S" then
		local s, p = unpack("<s4", data, pos)
		return s, p
	elseif tag == "B" then
		local len, count = unpack("<I4I4", data, pos)
		pos += 8
		local b = buffer.create(len)
		for _ = 1, count do
			local idx = unpack("<I4", data, pos)
			pos += 4
			local off = idx * PAGE
			local n = math.min(PAGE, len - off)
			buffer.writestring(b, off, string.sub(data, pos, pos + n - 1))
			pos += n
		end
		return b, pos
	elseif tag == "{" then
		local count = unpack("<I4", data, pos)
		pos += 4
		local t: { [any]: any } = {}
		for _ = 1, count do
			local k, v
			k, pos = decodeValue(data, pos)
			v, pos = decodeValue(data, pos)
			t[k] = v
		end
		return t, pos
	end
	error("snapshot: bad value tag at " .. tostring(pos - 1))
end

local function encodePath(path: { any }, out: { string })
	out[#out + 1] = pack("<I2", #path)
	for _, key in path do
		encodeValue(key, out, {})
	end
end

local function emitSet(path: { any }, value: any, out: { string })
	out[#out + 1] = "V"
	encodePath(path, out)
	encodeValue(value, out, {})
end

local function emitBufferDiff(path: { any }, live: buffer, ref: buffer, out: { string })
	local len = buffer.len(live)
	local pages: { string } = {}
	local count = 0
	local off = 0
	while off < len do
		local n = math.min(PAGE, len - off)
		local s = buffer.readstring(live, off, n)
		if s ~= buffer.readstring(ref, off, n) then
			count += 1
			pages[#pages + 1] = pack("<I4", off // PAGE)
			pages[#pages + 1] = s
		end
		off += PAGE
	end
	if count == 0 then
		return
	end
	out[#out + 1] = "D"
	encodePath(path, out)
	out[#out + 1] = pack("<I4I4", len, count)
	for _, p in pages do
		out[#out + 1] = p
	end
end

local function skippable(vt: string): boolean
	return vt == "function" or vt == "thread" or vt == "userdata" or vt == "vector"
end

local function walk(
	live: any,
	ref: any,
	path: { any },
	out: { string },
	visited: { [any]: boolean }
)
	for k, v in live do
		local kt = typeof(k)
		if kt == "string" or kt == "number" or kt == "boolean" then
			local vt = typeof(v)
			path[#path + 1] = k
			if vt == "table" then
				if not visited[v] then
					visited[v] = true
					local r = ref[k]
					if typeof(r) == "table" then
						walk(v, r, path, out, visited)
					else
						emitSet(path, v, out)
					end
				end
			elseif vt == "buffer" then
				if not visited[v] then
					visited[v] = true
					local r = ref[k]
					if typeof(r) == "buffer" and buffer.len(r) == buffer.len(v) then
						emitBufferDiff(path, v, r, out)
					else
						emitSet(path, v, out)
					end
				end
			elseif not skippable(vt) then
				if ref[k] ~= v then
					emitSet(path, v, out)
				end
			end
			path[#path] = nil
		end
	end
	for k, r in ref do
		local kt = typeof(k)
		if (kt == "string" or kt == "number" or kt == "boolean") and live[k] == nil then
			if not skippable(typeof(r)) then
				path[#path + 1] = k
				emitSet(path, nil, out)
				path[#path] = nil
			end
		end
	end
end

-- Records how `live` differs from `ref` (a machine freshly built the same way).
-- `extra` is any plain-data table the caller wants stored alongside (driver
-- state such as step counters); apply() hands it back.
function Snapshot.capture(live: any, ref: any, extra: any?): string
	local out: { string } = { MAGIC }
	encodeValue(extra or {}, out, {})
	walk(live, ref, {}, out, { [live] = true })
	return table.concat(out)
end

local function resolve(root: any, path: { any }): any
	local t = root
	for i = 1, #path - 1 do
		local nxt = t[path[i]]
		if typeof(nxt) ~= "table" then
			error("snapshot: path does not exist in the fresh machine")
		end
		t = nxt
	end
	return t
end

-- Overlays a checkpoint onto `target`, a machine built exactly like the
-- reference was. Returns the `extra` table that was captured.
function Snapshot.apply(target: any, data: string): any
	if string.sub(data, 1, #MAGIC) ~= MAGIC then
		error("snapshot: bad header")
	end
	local pos = #MAGIC + 1
	local extra
	extra, pos = decodeValue(data, pos)
	local size = #data
	while pos <= size do
		local tag = string.sub(data, pos, pos)
		pos += 1
		local n = unpack("<I2", data, pos)
		pos += 2
		local path: { any } = {}
		for i = 1, n do
			path[i], pos = decodeValue(data, pos)
		end
		local parent = resolve(target, path)
		local key = path[#path]
		if tag == "V" then
			local v
			v, pos = decodeValue(data, pos)
			parent[key] = v
		elseif tag == "D" then
			local len, count = unpack("<I4I4", data, pos)
			pos += 8
			local b = parent[key]
			if typeof(b) ~= "buffer" or buffer.len(b) ~= len then
				error(
					"snapshot: buffer mismatch against the fresh machine at "
						.. table.concat(path, ".")
						.. " (len "
						.. tostring(len)
						.. " vs "
						.. (if typeof(b) == "buffer" then tostring(buffer.len(b)) else typeof(b))
						.. ")"
				)
			end
			for _ = 1, count do
				local idx = unpack("<I4", data, pos)
				pos += 4
				local off = idx * PAGE
				local len2 = math.min(PAGE, len - off)
				buffer.writestring(b, off, string.sub(data, pos, pos + len2 - 1))
				pos += len2
			end
		else
			error("snapshot: bad op tag at " .. tostring(pos - 3))
		end
	end
	return extra
end

return Snapshot

-- Save: owns DataStore persistence of player state on join, leave, and server shutdown.
-- Server gameplay is authoritative; the client only renders and sends intents.
-- Public API: Save.load, Save.save, Save.saveAll, Save.bind, Save.startingCash
-- contract:
--   Owns: the lazily fetched "PulauBrainrot_v1" DataStore (looked up once), keys "p_" .. UserId.
--   pcall wrapped: GetDataStore (failure -> warn, store nil, session-only), GetAsync (failure -> warn, load returns nil),
--   SetAsync (failure -> warn, save returns false), each Save.save inside saveAll (failure -> warn, skip player), BindToClose (failure -> warn).
--   Validates: load returns the stored value only if it is a table; save needs a store and a PlayerState.serialize payload, stamps version = 1.
--   Returns: load -> table or nil; save -> boolean; startingCash -> Config.startingCash.
--   Refuses: retrying GetDataStore after the first attempt (storeReady latches even on failure); loading non-table
--   stored values (returns nil); saving with no store or no serialize payload (returns false); letting any DataStore
--   or BindToClose error escape to the caller (all are pcall wrapped and warned).
--   Does not own: the shape of player data (PlayerState.serialize builds it) or the starting cash value (Config owns it).
--   saveAll and bind return nothing; getStore is private and returns the cached store or nil.
--!strict

local DataStoreService = game:GetService("DataStoreService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

local Config = require(script.Parent:WaitForChild("Config"))
local PlayerState = require(script.Parent:WaitForChild("PlayerState"))

local STORE_NAME = "PulauBrainrot_v1"
local KEY_PREFIX = "p_"

local store: any = nil
local storeReady = false

-- getStore: fetches the "PulauBrainrot_v1" DataStore once under pcall, warning and caching nil on failure.
-- Returns the cached DataStore, or nil when DataStoreService is unavailable (session-only data).
local function getStore(): any
	if storeReady then
		return store
	end
	storeReady = true
	local ok, result = pcall(function()
		return DataStoreService:GetDataStore(STORE_NAME)
	end)
	if ok then
		store = result
	else
		store = nil
		warn("[Save] DataStore unavailable, session-only data: " .. tostring(result))
	end
	return store
end

local Save = {}

-- Save.load: reads the player's "p_" .. UserId record via a pcall wrapped GetAsync, warning on failure.
-- Returns the stored table, or nil when there is no store, the read fails, or the value is not a table.
function Save.load(player: Player): { [string]: any }?
	local dataStore = getStore()
	if not dataStore then
		return nil
	end
	local key = KEY_PREFIX .. tostring(player.UserId)
	local ok, result = pcall(function()
		return dataStore:GetAsync(key)
	end)
	if not ok then
		warn("[Save] load failed for " .. tostring(player.UserId) .. ": " .. tostring(result))
		return nil
	end
	if typeof(result) ~= "table" then
		return nil
	end
	return result
end

-- Save.save: serializes the player via PlayerState, stamps version = 1, and writes it with a pcall wrapped SetAsync.
-- Returns true on a successful write; false when there is no store, no payload, or SetAsync fails.
function Save.save(player: Player): boolean
	local dataStore = getStore()
	if not dataStore then
		return false
	end
	local payload = PlayerState.serialize(player)
	if not payload then
		return false
	end
	payload.version = 1
	local key = KEY_PREFIX .. tostring(player.UserId)
	local ok, err = pcall(function()
		dataStore:SetAsync(key, payload)
	end)
	if not ok then
		warn("[Save] save failed for " .. tostring(player.UserId) .. ": " .. tostring(err))
		return false
	end
	return true
end

-- Save.saveAll: calls Save.save for every connected player, each under pcall so one error skips only that player.
-- Returns nothing; per-player save results are discarded and errors are only warned.
function Save.saveAll()
	for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do
		local ok, err = pcall(function()
			Save.save(player)
		end)
		if not ok then
			warn("[Save] saveAll skipped " .. player.Name .. ": " .. tostring(err))
		end
	end
end

-- Save.bind: registers Save.saveAll as a game:BindToClose handler, warning if registration is unavailable.
-- Returns nothing.
function Save.bind()
	local ok, err = pcall(function()
		game:BindToClose(function()
			Save.saveAll()
		end)
	end)
	if not ok then
		warn("[Save] BindToClose unavailable: " .. tostring(err))
	end
end

-- Save.startingCash: exposes the configured starting cash for new or unsaved players.
-- Returns Config.startingCash as a number.
function Save.startingCash(): number
	return Config.startingCash
end

return Save

--!strict
-- Uart.lua -- 8250/16450 COM1 at 0x3F8-0x3FF.
--
-- The core only models the registers a DOS/Windows serial driver touches. Byte
-- I/O goes through an injected host backend so the module stays environment
-- pure: the Roblox client can wire a terminal, Lune tests use a loopback.

const band, bor, lshift = bit32.band, bit32.bor, bit32.lshift

const Uart = {}
Uart.__index = Uart

Uart.BASE = 0x3F8
Uart.RX_CAPACITY = 16

export type Backend = {
	writeByte: ((backend: any, value: number) -> ())?,
	readByte: ((backend: any) -> number?)?,
}

export type Uart = {
	backend: Backend?,
	rx: { number },
	overrun: boolean,
	threPending: boolean,
	ier: number,
	lcr: number,
	mcr: number,
	fcr: number,
	divisorLow: number,
	divisorHigh: number,
	scratch: number,
	new: (backend: Backend?) -> Uart,
	reset: (self: Uart) -> (),
	poll: (self: Uart) -> (),
	pushByte: (self: Uart, value: number) -> (),
	rxAvailable: (self: Uart) -> boolean,
	readByte: (self: Uart) -> number?,
	writeByte: (self: Uart, value: number) -> (),
	writeText: (self: Uart, text: string) -> (),
	irqPending: (self: Uart) -> boolean,
	interruptId: (self: Uart) -> number,
	lineStatus: (self: Uart) -> number,
	modemStatus: (self: Uart) -> number,
	in8: (self: Uart, port: number) -> number,
	out8: (self: Uart, port: number, value: number) -> (),
}

function Uart.new(backend: Backend?): Uart
	const self = setmetatable({}, Uart) :: any
	self.backend = backend
	self:reset()
	return self
end

function Uart.reset(self: Uart)
	self.rx = {}
	self.overrun = false
	self.threPending = true -- THR starts empty
	self.ier = 0
	self.lcr = 0x03 -- 8N1
	self.mcr = 0
	self.fcr = 0
	self.divisorLow = 12 -- 9600 with a 1.8432 MHz clock
	self.divisorHigh = 0
	self.scratch = 0
end

-- Pull one byte from the host backend. Called from the IRQ pump and on a
-- register read so polled and interrupt-driven guests both see input.
function Uart.poll(self: Uart)
	if #self.rx >= Uart.RX_CAPACITY then
		return
	end
	const backend = self.backend
	if not backend or not backend.readByte then
		return
	end
	const value = backend.readByte(backend)
	if value ~= nil then
		self.rx[#self.rx + 1] = band(value, 0xFF)
	end
end

function Uart.pushByte(self: Uart, value: number)
	self:poll()
	if #self.rx >= Uart.RX_CAPACITY then
		self.overrun = true
		return
	end
	self.rx[#self.rx + 1] = band(value, 0xFF)
end

function Uart.rxAvailable(self: Uart): boolean
	self:poll()
	return #self.rx > 0
end

function Uart.readByte(self: Uart): number?
	self:poll()
	if #self.rx == 0 then
		return nil
	end
	return table.remove(self.rx, 1)
end

-- A real 8250 in loopback returns TX to RX without touching the line. The
-- backend is only called for normal (non-loopback) transmission.
function Uart.writeByte(self: Uart, value: number)
	const byte = band(value, 0xFF)
	if band(self.mcr, 0x10) ~= 0 then
		self:pushByte(byte)
	else
		const backend = self.backend
		if backend and backend.writeByte then
			backend.writeByte(backend, byte)
		end
	end
	self.threPending = true
end

function Uart.writeText(self: Uart, text: string)
	for index = 1, #text do
		self:writeByte(string.byte(text, index) :: number)
	end
end

-- OUT2 (MCR bit 3) gates the card's IRQ line on a real PC.
function Uart.irqPending(self: Uart): boolean
	if band(self.mcr, 0x08) == 0 then
		return false
	end
	if band(self.ier, 0x01) ~= 0 then
		self:poll()
		if #self.rx > 0 then
			return true
		end
	end
	if band(self.ier, 0x02) ~= 0 and self.threPending then
		return true
	end
	return false
end

-- IIR: bit 0 = 0 means pending; bits 3-1 are the highest-priority source.
-- Reading IIR acknowledges a pending THRE interrupt.
function Uart.interruptId(self: Uart): number
	const fifo = if band(self.fcr, 0x01) ~= 0 then 0xC0 else 0
	const value = (function(): number
		if band(self.ier, 0x01) ~= 0 then
			self:poll()
			if #self.rx > 0 then
				return bor(fifo, 0x04) -- received data available
			end
		end
		if band(self.ier, 0x02) ~= 0 and self.threPending then
			return bor(fifo, 0x02) -- transmitter holding register empty
		end
		return 0x01
	end)()
	if band(value, 0x0E) == 0x02 then
		self.threPending = false
	end
	return value
end

function Uart.lineStatus(self: Uart): number
	self:poll()
	local status = 0x60 -- THRE and TEMT
	if #self.rx > 0 then
		status = bor(status, 0x01)
	end
	if self.overrun then
		status = bor(status, 0x02)
	end
	return status
end

function Uart.modemStatus(self: Uart): number
	if band(self.mcr, 0x10) ~= 0 then
		-- Loopback: CTS/DSR/RI/DCD mirror RTS/DTR/OUT1/OUT2.
		return lshift(band(self.mcr, 0x0F), 4)
	end
	return 0xB0 -- DCD, DSR and CTS asserted; no delta bits
end

function Uart.in8(self: Uart, port: number): number
	const offset = band(port - Uart.BASE, 0xFF)
	if offset == 0 then
		if band(self.lcr, 0x80) ~= 0 then
			return self.divisorLow
		end
		return self:readByte() or 0
	elseif offset == 1 then
		if band(self.lcr, 0x80) ~= 0 then
			return self.divisorHigh
		end
		return self.ier
	elseif offset == 2 then
		return self:interruptId()
	elseif offset == 3 then
		return self.lcr
	elseif offset == 4 then
		return self.mcr
	elseif offset == 5 then
		const status = self:lineStatus()
		self.overrun = false
		return status
	elseif offset == 6 then
		return self:modemStatus()
	elseif offset == 7 then
		return self.scratch
	end
	return 0
end

function Uart.out8(self: Uart, port: number, value: number)
	const byte = band(value, 0xFF)
	const offset = band(port - Uart.BASE, 0xFF)
	if offset == 0 then
		if band(self.lcr, 0x80) ~= 0 then
			self.divisorLow = byte
		else
			self:writeByte(byte) -- THR
		end
	elseif offset == 1 then
		if band(self.lcr, 0x80) ~= 0 then
			self.divisorHigh = byte
		else
			self.ier = band(byte, 0x0F)
		end
	elseif offset == 2 then
		self.fcr = byte
		if band(byte, 0x02) ~= 0 then -- clear receive FIFO
			self.rx = {}
			self.overrun = false
		end
	elseif offset == 3 then
		self.lcr = byte
	elseif offset == 4 then
		self.mcr = byte
	elseif offset == 7 then
		self.scratch = byte
	end
end

-- In-memory loopback backend: transmitted bytes come back as received bytes.
-- Tests use this, and it is a useful default for a host with no terminal.
function Uart.loopbackBackend(): Backend
	const queue: { number } = {}
	return {
		writeByte = function(_backend: any, value: number)
			queue[#queue + 1] = band(value, 0xFF)
		end,
		readByte = function(_backend: any): number?
			return table.remove(queue, 1)
		end,
	}
end

return Uart

-- Steal: owns stealing brainrot from another player's pedestal, including cooldowns, validity checks, and notices.
-- Server gameplay is authoritative; the client only renders and sends intents.
-- Public API: Steal.reason, Steal.try, Steal.clear, Steal.init, Steal.bind
-- contract:
--   Owns: per-thief cooldownUntil clock and the "StealPrompt" ProximityPrompts on every pedestal top.
--   Validates, in order: "missing" (no record or no owner), "owner" (thief owns the base), "cooldown", "locked" (Lock.baseLocked or
--   Bases.isLocked), "empty" (owner state missing or slot nil), "carrying" (thief state missing or already carrying; also when Carry.attach fails).
--   Returns: reason -> Reason; try -> (true, "ok") after moving the slot to the thief and notifying both, else (false, reason).
--   Note: try starts the thief's Config.stealCooldown before validating, so a refused attempt also starts the cooldown.
--!strict

local ProximityPromptService = game:GetService("ProximityPromptService")

local Config = require(script.Parent:WaitForChild("Config"))
local PlayerState = require(script.Parent:WaitForChild("PlayerState"))
local Bases = require(script.Parent:WaitForChild("Bases"))
local Carry = require(script.Parent:WaitForChild("Carry"))
local Lock = require(script.Parent:WaitForChild("Lock"))
local Pedestal = require(script.Parent:WaitForChild("Pedestal"))
local Storm = require(script.Parent:WaitForChild("Storm"))

local cooldownUntil: { [Player]: number } = {}

-- Steal module table.
-- Owns: the cooldownUntil map (thief -> os.clock() deadline, set by try, cleared by clear) and the
--   "StealPrompt" ProximityPrompt that init parents to every pedestal top in Bases.records().
-- Refuses: "missing" (no base record, no owner, or owner state gone), "owner" (thief owns the base),
--   "cooldown" (cooldownUntil[thief] > clock), "locked" (Lock.baseLocked or Bases.isLocked),
--   "empty" (owner slot nil), "carrying" (thief state missing, already carrying, or Carry.attach failed).
-- Returns: reason -> Reason; try -> (boolean, Reason), (true, "ok") only after the slot moves to the thief;
--   clear, init and bind return nothing; bind routes PromptTriggered on "StealPrompt" into Steal.try.
local Steal = {}

export type Reason = "ok" | "locked" | "empty" | "carrying" | "owner" | "cooldown" | "missing"

-- Checks, without changing state, whether thief may steal slotIndex from base baseIndex at now (or os.clock()).
-- Returns a Reason: "ok" when allowed, else the first failing check ("missing", "owner", "cooldown", "locked", "empty", "carrying").
function Steal.reason(thief: Player, baseIndex: number, slotIndex: number, now: number?): Reason
	local record = Bases.getByIndex(baseIndex)
	if not record or not record.owner then
		return "missing"
	end
	if record.owner == thief then
		return "owner"
	end
	local clock = now or os.clock()
	if (cooldownUntil[thief] or 0) > clock then
		return "cooldown"
	end
	if Lock.baseLocked(baseIndex, clock) or Bases.isLocked(record, clock) then
		return "locked"
	end
	local ownerState = PlayerState.get(record.owner)
	if not ownerState or ownerState.slots[slotIndex] == nil then
		return "empty"
	end
	local thiefState = PlayerState.get(thief)
	if not thiefState or thiefState.carrying ~= nil then
		return "carrying"
	end
	return "ok"
end

-- Starts the thief's cooldown, validates, then moves the owner's slot and pedestal model onto the thief and notifies both players.
-- Returns (true, "ok") on success, or (false, reason) with the owner's slot and model restored if Carry.attach fails.
function Steal.try(thief: Player, baseIndex: number, slotIndex: number, now: number?): (boolean, Reason)
	local clock = now or os.clock()
	cooldownUntil[thief] = clock + Config.stealCooldown
	local why = Steal.reason(thief, baseIndex, slotIndex, now)
	if why ~= "ok" then
		return false, why
	end
	local record = Bases.getByIndex(baseIndex)
	if not record or not record.owner then
		return false, "missing"
	end
	local owner = record.owner
	local ownerState = PlayerState.get(owner)
	if not ownerState then
		return false, "missing"
	end
	local slot = ownerState.slots[slotIndex]
	if not slot then
		return false, "empty"
	end
	local thiefState = PlayerState.get(thief)
	if not thiefState or thiefState.carrying ~= nil then
		return false, "carrying"
	end
	PlayerState.setSlot(owner, slotIndex, nil)
	local visual = Pedestal.visual(baseIndex, slotIndex)
	if visual and visual.model then
		local model = visual.model
		visual.model = nil
		local attached = Carry.attach(thief, slot, model)
		if not attached then
			PlayerState.setSlot(owner, slotIndex, slot)
			visual.model = model
			return false, "carrying"
		end
	else
		local attached = Carry.attach(thief, slot, nil)
		if not attached then
			PlayerState.setSlot(owner, slotIndex, slot)
			return false, "carrying"
		end
	end
	if visual then
		visual.sellPrompt.Enabled = false
		visual.placePrompt.Enabled = true
		visual.sellPrompt.ObjectText = "Empty"
	end
	cooldownUntil[thief] = (now or os.clock()) + Config.stealCooldown
	Storm.notify(owner, "stolen", tostring(thief.Name) .. " stole " .. tostring(slot.name) .. " from your base!", Color3.fromRGB(255, 110, 110))
	Storm.notify(thief, "stole", "You stole " .. tostring(slot.name) .. " from " .. tostring(owner.Name) .. "'s base!", Color3.fromRGB(255, 190, 90))
	return true, "ok"
end

-- Forgets the player's steal cooldown (e.g. when they leave).
-- Returns nothing.
function Steal.clear(player: Player)
	cooldownUntil[player] = nil
end

-- Creates a "StealPrompt" ProximityPrompt (hold Config.stealHold, range 10, no line of sight) on every pedestal top of every base.
-- Returns nothing.
function Steal.init()
	for _, record in Bases.records() do
		for slotIndex, top in record.pedestals do
			local prompt = Instance.new("ProximityPrompt")
			prompt.Name = "StealPrompt"
			prompt.ActionText = "Steal"
			prompt.ObjectText = "Brainrot"
			prompt.HoldDuration = Config.stealHold
			prompt.MaxActivationDistance = 10
			prompt.RequiresLineOfSight = false
			prompt.Parent = top
		end
	end
end

-- Finds which base and pedestal slot a prompt belongs to by matching its parent BasePart against every base's pedestals.
-- Returns (baseIndex, slotIndex), or (nil, nil) if the parent is not a BasePart or matches no pedestal.
local function slotOf(prompt: ProximityPrompt): (number?, number?)
	local top = prompt.Parent
	if not (top and top:IsA("BasePart")) then
		return nil, nil
	end
	for _, record in Bases.records() do
		for slotIndex, pedestal in record.pedestals do
			if pedestal == top then
				return record.index, slotIndex
			end
		end
	end
	return nil, nil
end

-- Connects ProximityPromptService.PromptTriggered so a triggered "StealPrompt" resolves its slot and calls Steal.try for the player.
-- Returns nothing.
function Steal.bind()
	ProximityPromptService.PromptTriggered:Connect(function(prompt, player)
		if prompt.Name ~= "StealPrompt" then
			return
		end
		local baseIndex, slotIndex = slotOf(prompt)
		if not baseIndex or not slotIndex then
			return
		end
		Steal.try(player, baseIndex, slotIndex)
	end)
end

return Steal

-- Vga.lua -- environment-pure VGA device model for RVPC.
--
-- The device owns the A0000..AFFFF aperture rather than Memory: a real VGA has
-- four 64 KiB planes behind one 64 KiB window, so the linear 1 MiB buffer
-- cannot represent it. Machine must route A0000..AFFFF accesses here and call
-- in8/out8 for 0x3C0..0x3DA. Unknown ports and registers latch instead of
-- faulting; VGA.DRV probes several of them during mode set.
--
-- Implemented: mode 12h (640x480x16 planar), mode 13h (320x200x256 linear),
-- text mode 3 fallback, write modes 0/1/2/3, read modes 0/1, set/reset,
-- enable set/reset, data rotate, logical operations, read map select, colour
-- compare/don't-care, bit mask, map mask, odd/even host addressing, CRTC
-- start/offset, attribute-controller palette selection (including AR14 colour
-- select), and DAC writes. Text mode 3 reads B8000 directly through mem and
-- does not use odd/even plane addressing. Mode 13h collapses chain-4 address
-- decode to a linear 64 KiB buffer; its write modes and bit mask are not
-- applied.
--
-- Mode 12h reads and writes decode the four planes at the same byte address.
-- Latches load on every aperture read. Write mode 3 always uses GC0 set/reset
-- (GC1 is ignored) and preserves bit-mask-zero bits from the latches, matching
-- VGA hardware. Odd/even host addressing is implemented for CPU reads/writes;
-- the CGA/EGA shift-register display formats are not. The CRTC 0x22 alias
-- exposes the four latches, as on real VGA hardware.
--
-- A guest VGA BIOS programs the controllers through I/O ports instead of
-- calling setMode, so syncLegacyMode infers text/planar/linear and the visible
-- geometry from GC6/AR10 and the CRTC registers. INT 10h AX=0012 therefore
-- reaches the planar renderer on its own.
--
-- Text mode 3 also models CRTC cursor start/end/location, the cursor
-- enable/disable bit, the text attribute blink phase, and the hardware cursor
-- in snapshots. Not implemented: sync timing, interlace/double-scan timing,
-- CGA/EGA 2bpp shift-register output, chain-2 memory, horizontal pel/byte
-- panning, split-screen line compare, the GC6 memory-map windows at
-- B0000/B8000, and the 256 KiB VGA memory map beyond the first 64 KiB.

local function decodeFont(): { [number]: { number } }
	local glyphs: { [number]: { number } } = {}
	for code = 32, 126 do
		const rows = table.create(8, 0) :: { number }
		const base = (code - 32) * 16 + 1
		for row = 0, 7 do
			const first = base + row * 2
			rows[row] = tonumber(string.sub(FONT_BYTES, first, first + 1), 16) or 0
		end
		glyphs[code] = rows
	end
	return glyphs
end

const FONT = decodeFont()

local function dac6To8(value: number): number
	const component = band(value, 0x3F)
	return bor(lshift(component, 2), rshift(component, 4))
end

local function rgbaWord(r: number, g: number, b: number): number
	return bor(bor(bor(r, lshift(g, 8)), lshift(b, 16)), 0xFF000000)
end

local function apertureOffset(addr: number): number
	if addr >= APERTURE_BASE then
		return band(addr - APERTURE_BASE, 0xFFFF)
	end
	return band(addr, 0xFFFF)
end

local function rotateRight(value: number, count: number): number
	if count == 0 then
		return band(value, 0xFF)
	end
	return band(bor(rshift(value, count), lshift(value, 8 - count)), 0xFF)
end

local function applyDataFunction(data: number, latch: number, fn: number): number
	if fn == 1 then
		return band(data, latch)
	elseif fn == 2 then
		return bor(data, latch)
	elseif fn == 3 then
		return bxor(data, latch)
	end
	return data
end
